terms.definition: Speed with a direction — displacement divided by time.
terms.function: Reports both how fast an object moves and which way, as one vector arrow.
terms.whereItIs: The rotating arrow above the car on the loop.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the vector partner of speed and the input required for acceleration and momentum.

terms.definition: A quantity that needs both a magnitude and a direction, drawn as an arrow.
terms.whyItMatters: Velocities, forces, and momentum all need arrows; vectors are how physics organizes all direction-carrying facts.
terms.whereItIs: Every arrow sprouted from a moving body.

terms.definition: A velocity change that occurs when the heading rotates, even when speed stays the same.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the reason constant speed on a curve still counts as changing velocity — and hence as acceleration.
terms.whereItIs: The compass ring and the arrow sweeping around as the car loops.

terms.definition: Velocity in the opposite direction to the positive reference, shown as a downward graph slope.
terms.whyItMatters: On a position-time graph a negative slope means the object is back-tracking toward its start.
terms.whereItIs: The reversed ghost arrow and the downward graph trace.
